reason: The text (Job 1:1-22) centers on Job, who is explicitly described as extraordinarily wealthy—possessing 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen, 500 female donkeys, and many servants. He is identified as 'great among all the people of the East,' establishing him as a wealthy patriarch and landowner, not a working person. The narrative is told about his circumstances and directly includes divine perspective (the conversation between God and Satan), neither of which represents the viewpoint of working or regular people.
